Marlie: Modern English-style variant of Marly or Marley, 'pleasant wood' in Old English, or a pet form of Marie or Marlene.
Naser: Arabic, from nasir 'helper, supporter'; variant spelling of Nasser or Nasir.
Norhane: Probably a North African (Arabic-influenced) coinage; possibly related to nur 'light'. Origin uncertain.
Stenn: Probably a modern Dutch or Flemish respelling of Sten, a Scandinavian short form meaning 'stone'. Origin uncertain.
Anastazja: Polish form of Anastasia, from Greek anastasis 'resurrection'.
Eslina: Probably a modern coined name, possibly blending Es- names such as Eslin or Selina. Origin uncertain.
Evann: Breton and Welsh-style variant of Evan or Ewan, from Welsh Ifan, ultimately Hebrew John, 'God is gracious'.
Flin: Probably a short form of Flynn, Irish, from Flann 'red, ruddy'. Origin uncertain.
Navaro: Probably from the Spanish surname Navarro, meaning 'from Navarre', itself of Basque origin 'plain among mountains'.
Penny: English short form of Penelope, Greek, possibly 'weaver' or 'duck' (penelops). Also used as a nickname for Penelope.
Sina: Boy's use is uncertain. Persian and Arabic Sina refers to Mount Sinai or Avicenna (Ibn Sina); in Germanic regions a short form of Rosina.
Syana: Probably a modern coined name, possibly a variant of Siana or Sayana; origin uncertain.
Vaiana: Polynesian (Tahitian), 'water of the sea' or 'cave water'; popularised by the Disney film Moana, known as Vaiana in Europe.
Vick: English short form of Victor or Vicky, from Latin victor 'conqueror'.
Em: Short form of Emma or Emily, from Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Enorah: Probably a variant of Enora or Honora, Breton form of Latin Honoria, 'honour'.
Jaylano: Modern coined name, combining the Jay- prefix with the Italian-style ending -ano.
Julya: Variant spelling of Julia, Latin, from the Roman family name Julius, possibly 'youthful'.
Luus: Dutch pet form of Lucia, Louise or Lucas; ultimately Latin lux 'light' (Lucia).
Lyem: Probably a respelling of Liam, Irish short form of Uilliam (William), 'resolute protector'.
Nejla: Turkish and Bosnian form of Arabic Najla, 'wide-eyed'.
Nohé: French-style variant of Noah, Hebrew Noach, usually explained as 'rest' or 'comfort'.
Othniel: Hebrew, 'lion of God' or 'strength of God'. A biblical judge of Israel.
Raïs: Arabic, 'chief, leader, head' (ra'is). Also spelled Rais or Raiss.
Tosca: Italian, 'Tuscan woman', from Toscana. Known from Puccini's opera Tosca.
Yacob: Variant of Jacob, Hebrew Ya'aqov, usually explained as 'holder of the heel' or 'may God protect'.
Yakoub: Arabic form of Jacob (Ya'qub), from Hebrew Ya'aqov, 'holder of the heel' or 'may God protect'.
Amany: Arabic, plural of umniyya, 'wishes, hopes, aspirations'.
Arwin: Probably a variant of Erwin or Arwen; Germanic 'friend of the army' or 'boar friend'. Origin uncertain.
Eliaz: Probably a variant of Elias, Greek form of Hebrew Eliyahu, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Enoah: Probably a blend of Enoch and Noah, or a respelling of Noah; Hebrew names meaning 'dedicated' and 'rest'. Origin uncertain.
Hüma: Turkish, from Persian Homa, a mythical bird of good fortune that brings happiness.
Licia: Italian short form of Felicia or Alicia, or a variant of Lycia; from Latin felix 'happy'. Origin partly uncertain.
Léonardo: French-accented form of Italian Leonardo, Germanic, 'brave as a lion'.
Mamady: West African (Mandinka and Susu), a local form of Muhammad, Arabic 'praiseworthy'.
Neema: Swahili, 'grace, favour, prosperity', from Arabic ni'ma.
Nihat: Turkish, from Arabic nihayat, 'end, limit'. Also a man's given name in Turkey.
Oswald: Old English, from os 'god' and weald 'rule', so 'divine power'. A Northumbrian saint-king.
Princess: English word name, from 'princess', a king's daughter; ultimately Latin princeps 'first, chief'.
Rifky: Yiddish form of Rivka (Rebecca), Hebrew, probably 'to tie, bind' or 'noose'.
Santi: Spanish short form of Santiago ('Saint James'), or Italian 'saints'; also Thai 'peace'.
Sebas: Spanish short form of Sebastián, from Greek sebastos 'venerable', meaning 'from Sebaste'.
Susie: English pet form of Susan or Susanna, from Hebrew shoshanna 'lily, rose'.
Thimeo: Modern variant of Timeo or Timothy, Greek timotheos 'honouring God'; possibly Dutch-style spelling.
Tymeo: Modern variant of Timeo or Timothy, Greek timotheos 'honouring God'. Possibly a coined form.
Alyne: Probably a variant of Aline or Alina, from Germanic adal 'noble'.
Arjun: Sanskrit, 'bright, white, clear'. The hero archer of the Mahabharata.
Caitlynn: Anglicised variant of Caitlin, Irish form of Catherine, from Greek katharos 'pure'.
Damin: Probably a variant of Damian, from Greek damazo 'to tame'; or Korean/Slavic variants. Origin uncertain.
Deon: Short form of Deonne or Dionysius, from Greek, 'follower of Dionysus'; also Afrikaans use via Dion.
Kymani: Probably Jamaican or African-American coinage, possibly 'adventurous traveller' in Jamaican use. Origin uncertain.
Maryama: Arabic and African form of Maryam (Mary), possibly Hebrew 'beloved' or 'bitter'.
Romayssae: Maghrebi spelling of Rumaysa, Arabic, a name of a Companion of the Prophet, possibly 'fragrant'.
Roxie: English pet form of Roxanne, from Persian Roshanak, 'little star' or 'dawn'.
Tesniem: Arabic Tasnim, a spring in Paradise, from sanama 'to rise high'. Maghrebi spelling.
Anfal: Arabic, 'spoils, gains'; the name of the eighth sura of the Quran.
Bianka: Variant of Bianca, Italian, 'white, fair'. Also a Polish, Hungarian and German form.
Ferdaws: Arabic Firdaws, 'paradise, garden', from Persian pardis.
Jed: Short form of Jedidiah, Hebrew, 'beloved of God'; also an English pet form of Jedediah.
Lyssia: Probably a modern variant of Alyssa or Lysia, possibly from Greek lysis 'release'. Origin uncertain.
Maciej: Polish form of Matthias, from Hebrew Mattityahu, 'gift of God'.
Noomi: Variant of Naomi, Hebrew, 'pleasantness'. Also a Finnish and Estonian spelling.
Seyyid: Turkish form of Arabic sayyid, 'lord, master'; a title for descendants of the Prophet.
Tefan: Probably a shortened form of Stefan, from Greek stephanos 'crown, wreath'. Origin uncertain.
Tisse: Probably a Dutch or Frisian short form; origin uncertain, possibly from Matthijs/Matthias or Tijs.
Violeta: Spanish, Portuguese and Eastern European form of Violet, from Latin viola, the flower.
Ahmadou: West African (French-speaking) form of Ahmad, Arabic, 'most praised'.
Arlinda: Probably Albanian or Portuguese, possibly from Germanic Arlind; or a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Eleysa: Probably a modern coined variant of Elisa or Elysa, from Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
Lonore: Variant or shortening of Eléonore (Eleanor), possibly from Provençal Aliénor; origin debated.
Louey: Modern spelling of Louis or Louie, from Germanic Chlodovech, 'famous warrior'.
Lyham: Probably a respelling of Liam or a variant of Lyam; Irish short form of William. Origin uncertain.
Maélyne: Modern French blend of Maël (Breton 'prince, chief') and the ending -yne or -line.
Milia: Probably a short form of Emilia or Camilia, from Latin Aemilius. Origin uncertain.
Nikol: Czech and Bulgarian form of Nicole, from Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'.
Pifte: Origin uncertain; probably a rare or coined name, possibly of African or Eastern European origin.
Seydina: West African (Senegal), from Arabic sayyidina, 'our master', a title for the Prophet and his companions.
Skylar: English, from Dutch Schuyler, 'scholar' or 'shelter'; modern given name, mostly American.
Stieg: Scandinavian and German, from Old Norse stigr 'path, way', or a short form of Stigand.
Taho: Probably a rare or coined name; origin uncertain. Possibly Japanese or African in origin.
Tyas: Probably a Dutch-style variant of Thijs or Tijs, short forms of Matthijs; or a Javanese name. Origin uncertain.
Tymoteusz: Polish form of Timothy, from Greek timotheos, 'honouring God'.
Auxence: French form of Auxentius, from Greek auxanein, 'to increase, grow'. A saint's name.
Dastan: Persian and Central Asian, 'tale, epic story'.
Douha: Arabic duha, 'forenoon, morning brightness'; the title of the 93rd sura of the Quran.
Elric: Old English, from ael 'elf' or aethel 'noble' and ric 'ruler', so 'noble ruler'.
Elèna: French-accented form of Helena or Elena, from Greek, perhaps 'torch' or 'bright one'.
Esben: Danish, from Old Norse Asbjorn, 'god bear' (as 'god' and bjorn).
Fallone: Probably a variant of the French surname Fallon or Italian Fallone; origin uncertain.
Fatimatou: West African form of Fatima, Arabic, 'one who abstains' or 'weaned'. The daughter of the Prophet.
Habibatou: West African form of Habiba, Arabic, 'beloved' (feminine).
Iva: Slavic, short form of Ivana, or a form of the willow (iva); also a form of Eve. Feminine of Ivan, 'God is gracious'.
Jailey: Modern American coinage, a blend of Jay and Hailey or Kayley; origin uncertain.
Keza: Rwandan (Kinyarwanda), 'beautiful'; also Hungarian as a short form of Kázmér.
Maelya: Modern French coinage, from Maël (Breton 'prince') with the feminine ending -ya.
Marly: Variant of Marley, English, 'pleasant wood', or short form of Marlene. Used as a girl's name.
Nicolò: Italian form of Nicholas, Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'.
Queen: English word name for a female monarch, from Old English cwen 'woman, wife'.
Tylian: Probably a modern coined name, blending Tyler or Tyl with -ian; origin uncertain.
Williams: English patronymic surname turned first name, 'son of William', from Germanic 'resolute protector'.
Youmna: Arabic Yumna, 'good fortune, blessing'; from yumn, 'luck'.
Cattleya: Orchid genus named after William Cattley, an English horticulturist, used as a rare girl's name.
Delio: Italian and Spanish, 'of Delos', the Greek island of Apollo's birth; also a short form of Candelario.
Idiatou: West African (Guinean) form of Idia or Aidia; origin uncertain, possibly Arabic-influenced.
Kaissy: Probably a modern variant of Kaisy or Kassie, a pet form of Cassandra; origin uncertain.
Kamilla: Feminine form of Camillus, Latin, 'young attendant at a religious rite'. Common in Scandinavia, Poland and Hungary.
Leïna: Probably a variant of Lena or Leila; Lena is a short form of Helena or Magdalena.
Lourenço: Portuguese form of Laurence, from Latin Laurentius, 'from Laurentum' or 'laurel'.
Lyséa: Probably a modern coined name, possibly from Greek lysis 'release' or Lysia. Origin uncertain.
Mikhail: Russian and Arabic form of Michael, Hebrew, 'who is like God?'.
Miliano: Italian, from Emiliano or Maximilian, Latin Aemilianus 'rival' or Maximus 'greatest'.
Niccolò: Italian form of Nicholas, Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'; as in Machiavelli.
Riva: Italian and Hebrew; Italian 'river bank', and a Hebrew form of Rebecca, probably 'to tie'.
Sedra: Arabic, 'lote tree', from Sidrat al-Muntaha in the Quran; also a Hebrew 'weekly Torah portion'.
Sohane: Modern name, perhaps a variant of Sohan (Sanskrit/Hindi 'beautiful') or Soane; origin uncertain.
Umeyr: Turkish form of Arabic Umayr, 'long-lived', or diminutive of Umar. A Companion's name.
Aidy: Pet form of Aidan or Aideen, from Irish Aodhán, 'little fire'.
Aly: Short form of Ali, Arabic, 'exalted, high'; also a pet form of Alison or Alexandra.
Beril: Turkish, from Beryl, Greek beryllos, the gemstone beryl.
Cathaleya: Variant of Cattleya, an orchid named after William Cattley; a rare modern girl's name.
Chavi: Hebrew Chavi, from chavah 'to live', or a modern Indian name from chhavi 'image, radiance'.
Hadiatou: West African form of Hadiya or Hadia, Arabic, 'gift' or 'guide'.
Katalyna: Variant of Katalina or Catalina, Spanish form of Catherine, from Greek katharos 'pure'.
Kaylin: Modern American coinage, a blend of Kay and -lyn; possibly from Caitlin. Origin uncertain.
Khady: West African (Senegal), Wolof form of Khadija, Arabic, 'premature child'. The Prophet's first wife.
Lilianna: Elaborated form of Lilian or Liliana, possibly from Latin lilium 'lily' or Elizabeth.
Maysen: Modern English-style variant of Mason, 'stone worker', from Old French maçon.
Mikoaj: Polish Mikołaj with a lost letter; form of Nicholas, Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'.
Oriano: Italian, probably from Latin Orianus or from Oriana, possibly 'golden' (aurum). Origin uncertain.
Shulem: Yiddish, from Hebrew shalom, 'peace'. A Hasidic given name.
Sofija: Serbian, Croatian, Lithuanian and Latvian form of Sophia, Greek, 'wisdom'.
Soën: Probably a modern variant of Soen or Sven; or a Breton/Dutch coinage. Origin uncertain.
Thymeo: Modern variant of Timeo or Timothy, Greek timotheos 'honouring God'; probably a coined spelling.
Ylann: Probably a Breton-style respelling of Ylan or Ilan, Hebrew 'tree' (ilan).
Aalyah: Variant of Aaliyah, Arabic, 'exalted, sublime'; also Hebrew aliyah 'ascent'.
Anthime: French form of Anthimus, from Greek anthemon, 'flowery, blooming'. A saint's name.
Aurélio: Portuguese and Spanish form of Aurelius, Latin, 'golden'.
Eyup: Turkish form of Ayyub (Job), Arabic and Hebrew, possibly 'persecuted' or 'repentant'.
Ilara: Probably a coined variant of Ilaria, Italian from Latin hilaris 'cheerful'. Origin uncertain.
Ilyane: Probably a modern variant of Ilyan or Elian, ultimately Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Izïa: Probably a modern French coinage, possibly from Isia or Izia, variants linked to Isis or Isabella. Origin uncertain.
Kadiata: West African form of Khadija, Arabic, 'premature child'; the first wife of the Prophet.
Layanah: Arabic, 'softness, gentleness' (layana); Layan with a feminine ending.
Leea: Probably a variant of Lia or Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'. Also Finnish Leea.
Lillo: Italian pet form of Basilio or Pasquale, or from Lilly; origin varies by use.
Mehran: Persian, from mehr 'sun, kindness' and -an, 'kind, loving'.
Nare: Armenian, probably a feminine name meaning 'delicate, fair'; also a variant of Nari. Origin uncertain.
Toulouse: From the French city, of Gaulish or Roman origin (Tolosa); a rare given name.
Ysia: Probably a variant of Isia or Ysée; possibly from Greek, 'healthy'. Origin uncertain.
Zaza: Georgian short form of Zakaria, Hebrew 'God remembers'; also an affectionate pet name.
Anemone: From the flower name, Greek anemos 'wind', literally 'daughter of the wind'.
Aélia: French form of Aelia, a Roman family name, Latin from Greek helios, 'sun'.
Aïnhoa: Basque, from Ainhoa, a village and a Marian shrine name; meaning uncertain, possibly 'dwelling place of flowers'.
Cali: Probably a short form of Calista or Caliana, or from California; also Somali 'Cali' as a form of Ali.
Cass: Short form of Cassandra, Greek, 'shining upon man', or Cassius, Latin, 'hollow'. Used for both sexes.
Diyana: Variant of Diana, Latin, 'divine, heavenly'; also a Bulgarian and Malay form.
Duha: Arabic, 'forenoon, morning brightness'; the title of the 93rd sura of the Quran.
Elaïa: Probably a modern variant based on Greek elaia, 'olive tree'. Origin uncertain.
Erduan: Albanian form of Erdogan or Erdoan, Turkish Erdoğan, 'brave falcon'. Origin partly uncertain.
Erturul: Turkish Ertuğrul with a lost character, 'brave and firm', from er 'man' and tuğrul 'hawk'.
King: English word name, from Old English cyning, 'king, ruler'.
Kyliano: Modern coined name, a mix of Kylian (Irish Cillian, 'little church' or 'war') with the Italian ending -iano.
Linah: Arabic Lina, 'tender, soft'; also a variant of Lina, a short form of names ending -lina.
Milàn: Variant of Milan, Slavic mil, 'dear, gracious'; also a city in northern Italy.
Nateo: Probably a variant of Mateo or Natan, Hebrew 'gift'. Origin uncertain.
Oumaya: North African spelling of Umayya or Oumaima, Arabic, 'little mother' (diminutive of umm).
Rayden: Modern English invented name, possibly from Raiden or Raydan; origin uncertain. Also Japanese 'thunder god'.
Renesmee: Invented by Stephenie Meyer for Twilight, a blend of Renée and Esmé.
Sayfeddine: Arabic Sayf al-Din, 'sword of the faith'.
Thelio: Probably a modern coined name; possibly a variant of Elio or Thelonious. Origin uncertain.
Zach: Short form of Zachary, Hebrew Zekharyah, 'the Lord remembers'.
Zenab: Variant of Zeinab or Zaynab, Arabic, a fragrant tree and a name of the Prophet's daughter.
Abdulaziz: Arabic Abd al-Aziz, 'servant of the Almighty' (al-Aziz is a name of God).
Batoul: Arabic Batul, 'virgin, devoted woman'; epithet of Fatima.
Buglem: Origin uncertain; probably a rare or coined name, perhaps Turkish-influenced.
Felicity: English, from Latin felicitas, 'good fortune, happiness'.
Filemon: Polish, Czech and Greek form of Philemon, Greek, 'affectionate'. A biblical recipient of Paul's letter.
Göktug: Turkish Göktuğ, from gök 'sky' and tuğ 'standard, banner'.
Inaïa: Probably a variant of Inaya, Arabic, 'care, concern, providence'.
Matylda: Polish and Czech form of Matilda, Germanic, 'mighty in battle'.
Rubi: Spanish and English form of Ruby, the red gemstone, from Latin rubeus 'red'.
Ryo: Japanese, depending on the kanji, 'refreshing', 'dragon' or 'excellent'.
Théana: Probably from Greek theana, 'divine' or 'goddess' (thea), an old Greek female name.
Victory: English word name meaning 'triumph', from Latin victoria.
Éthan: French form of Ethan, Hebrew, 'strong, firm, enduring'.
